author: jvranek
content: the PRs keep only the highest when you configure it to send multiple requests. if it's another config option to select between `latest` and `highest` that still puts you in regime A since builders wouldn't be able to trust the average proposer

author: potuz
content: again there is zero point in requesting multiple bids with "latest", for that matter just request later and once.

author: vladimir_ea
content: Requesting multiple bids from a builder / relay and selecting the highest value bid would be considered somewhat adversarial from a builder point of view.

author: nflaig
content: so you are saying selecting the highest bid as a proposer is adversarial? that's seems rather rationale to me, on the other hand, [adjusting the bid](https://github.com/ultrasoundmoney/relay-docs/blob/main/builders/bid-adjustment.md) to pay the proposer less and pocket the extra money yourself I rather see as "adversarial" towards the proposer

author: potuz
content: I don't want to end up in a discussion about modeling the auction, I think our role is to give options to operators and let them choose what they do. I think clients should all give more or less the same options with the same feature flags. Unfortunately we are stupid enough that when trying to standardize these things we would get into neverending bike shedding and never get anywhere, so I am hoping that other clients copy our design on the circuit breaker and the feature flags for bid selection, or otherwise that we copy theirs, but eventually we converge on the same set.

author: vladimir_ea
content: fair enough, in the absence of bike-shedding, i expect builders will also unilaterally decide how to behave.

author: vladimir_ea
content: The consequence is that the options you are giving to operators might not do what they say on the tin: for example, if you give the operator the option to make multiple bid requests and select the highest and builders decide to only respond to one bid request (which seems like the logical thing to do) - then the consequence is that the operator in effect picks a single early bid and is not in fact choosing the highest bid out of several.

author: potuz
content: That I think is for operators and builders to sort out, we are giving the options so that no forks occur over this

author: jvranek
content: If you mean forked BNs that isn’t necessary since a sophisticated operator can more easily fork a sidecar. My argument though was that doing the job for them puts us into this regime that’s worse
